description: The International Labour Organization (ILO) is devoted to promoting social justice and internationally recognized human and labour rights, pursuing its founding mission that social justice is essential to universal and lasting peace. As the only tripartite UN agency, the ILO set labour standards, develop policies and devise programmes promoting decent work for all women and men.

The International Institute for Labour Studies was established in 1960 as an autonomous facility of the International Labour Organisation. Its mandate was to promote policy research and public discussion on emerging issues of concern to the ILO and its constituents: labour, business and government. It was dissolved in 2014.

description: The Interim Commission for the International Trade Organization (ICITO) was established by a Resolution of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Employment (the Havana Conference) “considering that pending the establishment of the Organization certain interim functions should be performed”. December 1950 the United States Department of State issued a statement of policy indicating that the Havana Charter would not be submitted again to the United States Congress. It subsequently became evident that the establishment of the ITO would be indefinitely postponed. Since then, ICITO has served as the GATT secretariat: https://www.wto.org/gatt_docs/English/SULPDF/90180004.pdf

description: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is the only global international organization dealing with the rules of trade between nations. the WTO operates a global system of trade rules, it acts as a forum for negotiating trade agreements, it settles trade disputes between its members and it supports the needs of developing countries.

The ITC supports the international competitiveness of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) in developing countries and transition economies. As a joint agency of the United Nations and the World Trade Organization, it focuses on sustainable development, inclusive economic growth, and poverty reduction through trade.

WMO fosters international cooperation to improve meteorological, climatological, hydrological and environmental observations. It facilitates exchange of information and develops services to protect lives and property from natural hazards and to contribute to socioeconomic well-being.

The WMO supports global scientific cooperation on the Earth's atmosphere, climate, and water resources. It facilitates worldwide networks for the rapid exchange of weather, climate, and hydrological data, improve multi-hazard early warning systems, establish international standards and practices for meteorological observations and performance, applyi atmospheric and hydrological sciences to key areas like agriculture, aviation, shipping, and water management.

Established in 1988 by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), the body operates to inform global climate policy. [1, 2, 3, 4]
